subproblem.title: A nonempty embedded d-dimensional submanifold of ℝ^P has d ≤ P
subproblem.statement: Let P, d, r ∈ ℕ and let M ⊆ ℝ^P be a nonempty d-dimensional embedded C^r submanifold in the sense of the contract (IsEmbeddedSubmanifold r d M: every y ∈ M has an open V ⊆ ℝ^d, an open W ∋ y and ψ : ℝ^d → ℝ^P, C^r and injective on V, with ψ(V) = W ∩ M, V ∩ ψ⁻¹(K) compact for compact K ⊆ W, and Dψ(z) injective for every z ∈ V). Then d ≤ P.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P d r : ℕ) (M : Set (Euclid P)), IsEmbeddedSubmanifold r d M → M.Nonempty → d ≤ P
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof step 1 (k ≥ 1), stated for an arbitrary nonempty embedded submanifold. The parent applies it with P := n + k, d := n + 1, r := 2, M := N (N ≠ ∅ because N ∩ U ≠ ∅ by InClassO) and concludes 1 ≤ k from n + 1 ≤ n + k.
1. Since M is nonempty, pick y ∈ M.
2. By IsEmbeddedSubmanifold r d M at y there are sets V ⊆ ℝ^d and W ⊆ ℝ^P and a map ψ : ℝ^d → ℝ^P such that y ∈ W, ψ(V) = W ∩ M, and Dψ(z) = fderiv ℝ ψ z : ℝ^d → ℝ^P is injective for every z ∈ V. (The remaining chart properties — openness, C^r regularity, injectivity of ψ on V, properness — are not needed.)
3. Since y ∈ W and y ∈ M, we have y ∈ W ∩ M = ψ(V), so there is z ∈ V (with ψ(z) = y).
4. Dψ(z) is an injective ℝ-linear map from ℝ^d to the finite-dimensional space ℝ^P. The dimension of the domain of an injective linear map is at most the dimension of its codomain (Mathlib LinearMap.finrank_le_finrank_of_injective), so finrank ℝ^d ≤ finrank ℝ^P.
5. Since finrank ℝ (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin q)) = q for every q (finrank_euclideanSpace_fin), step 4 reads d ≤ P.
proof_key_steps: Pick y ∈ M and a chart (V, W, ψ) of M at y.
y ∈ W ∩ M = ψ(V) yields a point z ∈ V.
Dψ(z) : ℝ^d → ℝ^P is an injective linear map, so d = finrank ℝ^d ≤ finrank ℝ^P = P.

audit.reason: Prose and Lean type match, including nonemptiness and arbitrary regularity r. A chart at a carrier point supplies a nonempty parameter domain and an injective differential; finrank monotonicity gives d ≤ P. The proof is complete and non-circular.

subproblem.title: ∂[[E]] is a cycle: ∂∂[[E]] = 0
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let U, E ⊆ ℝ^P, let ξ_N : ℝ^P → Λ_{n+1}(ℝ^P) be arbitrary, and let T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) satisfy T(ω) = ∫_E ⟨dω, ξ_N⟩ dH^{n+1} for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) (IsBoundaryOfRegion T E ξ_N). Then ∂T = 0 in U (BoundaryVanishes T; for n = 0 this is Simon's convention ∂T = 0).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U E : Set (Euclid P)) (ξN : Euclid P → MultiVector P (n + 1)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n), IsBoundaryOfRegion T E ξN → BoundaryVanishes T
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof step 3 (∂T = 0; Simon (6.1.12) d∘d = 0 and 7.5.1 T = ∂[[E]]), stated for an arbitrary ambient dimension P and arbitrary U, E, ξ_N.
1. If n = 0, BoundaryVanishes T is True by definition (Simon's convention ∂T = 0 for 0-currents), and there is nothing to prove.
2. Let n = m + 1. We show T.boundary = 0 by extensionality of currents (GeometricCurrentOn.ext): fix φ ∈ 𝒟^m(U). By the definition of the boundary (6.2.3), ∂T(φ) = T(dφ), where dφ ∈ 𝒟^{m+1}(U) is the exterior derivative of φ as a test form in U (exteriorDerivativeTestOn).
3. Applying IsBoundaryOfRegion to the test form dφ gives T(dφ) = ∫_E ξ_N(z)(d(dφ)(z)) dH^{m+2}(z).
4. Since φ is smooth, d(dφ) = 0 (Simon (6.1.12); SimonGMT exteriorDerivative_sq). Hence ξ_N(z)(d(dφ)(z)) = ξ_N(z)(0) = 0 for every z by linearity of ξ_N(z), and the integral in 3 equals 0.
5. Therefore ∂T(φ) = 0 = 0(φ) for every φ, i.e. T.boundary = 0, which is BoundaryVanishes T for n = m + 1.
proof_key_steps: For n = 0, BoundaryVanishes T is True by definition.
For n = m + 1, ∂T(φ) = T(dφ) = ∫_E ξ_N(d(dφ)) dH^{m+2}.
d(dφ) = 0 for smooth φ, so the integrand and the integral vanish, and T.boundary = 0 by extensionality.

audit.reason: The proposition matches the prose, including arbitrary U and E. Degree zero is definitionally True; in successor degree, testing the boundary and applying d² = 0 proves equality with the zero current. No openness, measurability or unstated hypothesis is needed.

subproblem.title: ∂[[E]] is supported in N when E ⊆ N and (N̄∖N) ∩ U = ∅
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open, let N, E ⊆ ℝ^P with (N̄ ∖ N) ∩ U = ∅ and E ⊆ N, let ξ_N : ℝ^P → Λ_{n+1}(ℝ^P) be arbitrary, and let T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) satisfy T(ω) = ∫_E ⟨dω, ξ_N⟩ dH^{n+1} for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) (IsBoundaryOfRegion T E ξ_N). Then spt T ⊆ N.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U N E : Set (Euclid P)) (ξN : Euclid P → MultiVector P (n + 1)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n), IsOpen U → (closure N \ N) ∩ U = ∅ → E ⊆ N → IsBoundaryOfRegion T E ξN → T.support ⊆ N
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof step 2 (spt T ⊆ N; Simon 7.5, chapter-07.txt lines 746–780, T = ∂[[E]] with E ⊆ N), stated for an arbitrary ambient dimension P. Notation: tsupport ω is the closed support of a form; Z(T) (zeroRegion) is the union of all open W with closure W compact, closure W ⊆ U and T(ω) = 0 for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W; spt T = U ∖ Z(T).
1. Let x ∈ spt T. Then x ∈ U and x ∉ Z(T). Suppose, for a contradiction, that x ∉ N.
2. x ∉ closure N: otherwise x ∈ (closure N ∖ N) ∩ U, which is empty by hypothesis.
3. U ∖ closure N is open (U is open and closure N is closed) and contains x, so there is ε > 0 with ball(x, ε) ⊆ U ∖ closure N. Put W₀ := ball(x, ε/2). W₀ is open, and closure W₀ = closedBall(x, ε/2) is compact (Heine–Borel in ℝ^P) and contained in ball(x, ε) ⊆ U.
4. T vanishes on W₀. Let ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W₀. Exterior differentiation does not enlarge the topological support (SimonGMT tsupport_exteriorDerivative_subset), so tsupport(dω) ⊆ tsupport ω ⊆ W₀ ⊆ ball(x, ε). Let z ∈ E. Then z ∈ N ⊆ closure N, so z ∉ ball(x, ε), hence z ∉ tsupport(dω) and dω(z) = 0; therefore ξ_N(z)(dω(z)) = ξ_N(z)(0) = 0 because ξ_N(z) is linear. Thus the integrand in T(ω) = ∫_E ξ_N(z)(dω(z)) dH^{n+1}(z) (IsBoundaryOfRegion) vanishes at every point of E, and T(ω) = 0. (A set integral of a function vanishing at every point of the integration set is 0, with no measurability assumption on E: Mathlib setIntegral_eq_zero_of_forall_eq_zero.)
5. By 3 and 4, W₀ belongs to the family whose union is Z(T); as x ∈ W₀, x ∈ Z(T). This contradicts x ∉ Z(T). Hence x ∈ N, and spt T ⊆ N.
proof_key_steps: A point x ∈ spt T ∖ N lies in U and, by (N̄∖N) ∩ U = ∅, outside N̄.
A ball W₀ = ball(x, ε/2) with ball(x, ε) ⊆ U ∖ N̄ is open with compact closure in U.
For tsupport ω ⊆ W₀, tsupport dω ⊆ tsupport ω misses E ⊆ N, so the integrand ξ_N(dω) vanishes on E and T(ω) = 0.
Hence x ∈ W₀ ⊆ Z(T), contradicting x ∈ spt T = U ∖ Z(T).

audit.reason: All hypotheses match the exact type. The closure condition and openness provide a relatively compact neighborhood disjoint from N. Exterior differentiation preserves the required support bound, making the integrand zero on E. The cited integral lemma requires no measurability of E. The zero-region contradiction proves the conclusion without sibling or parent reliance.

subproblem.title: A 0-current minimizing in A with support in A has empty regular set
subproblem.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open, let A ⊆ ℝ^P, and let T ∈ 𝒟_0(U) be minimizing in A in the sense of the contract (IsMinimizingIn T A, Simon 7.1.1: T is integer multiplicity, and M_W(T) ≤ M_W(S) for every open W with closure W compact and ⊆ U and every integer multiplicity S ∈ 𝒟_0(U) with spt(S − T) a compact subset of A ∩ W; the condition ∂S = ∂T is vacuous in degree 0). If spt T ⊆ A, then reg T = ∅ (regularSet T = ∅, Simon 7.4.1 as frozen in the contract).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (U A : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U 0), IsOpen U → IsMinimizingIn T A → T.support ⊆ A → regularSet T = ∅
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof step 4 (4.1–4.8: for n = 0 a regular point is an isolated atom of T, and deleting it gives a cheaper admissible competitor), with the parent's set N ∩ U replaced by an arbitrary A satisfying spt T ⊆ A. The parent applies this lemma with P := 0 + k and A := N ∩ U, using spt T ⊆ N (its step 2) and spt T ⊆ U. Notation: H^0 = μHE[0]; tsupport ω is the closed support of a form; Z(S) (zeroRegion) is the union of all open W with closure W compact, closure W ⊆ U, on which S vanishes, and spt S = U ∖ Z(S); M_W(S) (massOn) is the supremum of ofReal(S(ω)) over ω ∈ 𝒟^0(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W and Euclidean coefficient norm ≤ 1 at every point.

0. Facts in dimension 0.
 (F1) H^0 = μHE[0] = μH[0] (Mathlib euclideanHausdorffMeasure_zero) and H^0({x}) = 1 for every x (hausdorffMeasure_zero_singleton). Hence H^0(F) = #F for finite F (additivity over the measurable singletons), and every set S with H^0(S) < ∞ is finite (otherwise it contains finite subsets of every cardinality). Moreover, for any set C and any x ∈ C, (H^0⌞C)({x}) = H^0({x} ∩ C) = 1 ({x} is measurable), so by monotonicity no (H^0⌞C)-null set contains a point of C.
 (F2) Fin 0 → ℝ^P has exactly one element, the empty family, written (); for a 0-covector α write α() for its value at (). Let ε₀ be the 0-covector with ε₀() = 1 (the constant alternating map, constOfIsEmpty).
 (F3) The Euclidean coefficient norm of a 0-covector α is |α()|: the only index map Fin 0 → Fin P is the empty one, which is strictly monotone, so the defining sum has the single term α()².
 (F4) If ξ' ∈ Λ_0(ℝ^P) satisfies IsUnitOrientationOf ξ' Q for some subspace Q, its frame τ : Fin 0 → ℝ^P is the empty family, so either ξ'(α) = α() for all α or ξ'(α) = −α() for all α; write ξ'(α) = s·α() with s ∈ {1, −1}.
 (F5) For z ∈ ℝ^P and a > 0 there is a smooth g : ℝ^P → [0, 1] with g(z) = 1 and g = 0 outside ball(z, a), so tsupport g ⊆ closedBall(z, a) (a ContDiffBump centred at z with outer radius a). For c ∈ ℝ the 0-form ω := c g ε₀ (x ↦ c g(x) ε₀) is smooth with compact support, tsupport ω ⊆ closedBall(z, a), ω(x)() = c g(x), and its coefficient norm at x is |c| g(x) by (F3); if closedBall(z, a) ⊆ U then ω ∈ 𝒟^0(U).

1. (Set-up.) Suppose, for a contradiction, that y ∈ reg T. By the first conjunct of IsMinimizingIn, T is integer multiplicity; fix R ∈ IMRep U 0 with R.Represents T, with carrier C (Borel, C ⊆ U, countably 0-rectifiable), multiplicity θ (measurable, ℕ-valued, θ ≥ 1 on C, ∫_{C∩K} θ dH^0 < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U) and orientation ξ_R. Thus T(ω) = ∫_C θ(x) ξ_R(x)(ω(x)) dH^0(x) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^0(U).

2. (Local form of T near y; parent 4.1.) By the definition of regularSet there are ρ > 0 with ball(y, ρ) ⊆ U, m ∈ ℤ ∖ {0}, a set M with y ∈ M and ξ : ℝ^P → Λ_0(ℝ^P) such that IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 1 0 M, IsOrientation 0 M ξ, and T(ω) = m ∫_M ξ(x)(ω(x)) dH^0(x) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^0(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ ball(y, ρ).
 2a. The chart of M at y gives V ⊆ ℝ^0, an open W_M ⊆ ℝ^P with y ∈ W_M, and ψ : ℝ^0 → ℝ^P with ψ(V) = W_M ∩ M. As ℝ^0 = {0}, ψ(V) ⊆ {ψ(0)}; since y ∈ W_M ∩ M = ψ(V), y = ψ(0) and W_M ∩ M = {y}.
 2b. Choose r with 0 < r < ρ and ball(y, r) ⊆ W_M (W_M is open). Then M ∩ ball(y, r) = {y}.
 2c. By IsOrientation 0 M ξ at y ∈ M and (F4), ξ(y)(α) = s·α() for all α, for some s ∈ {1, −1}.
 2d. Claim (*): every ω ∈ 𝒟^0(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ ball(y, r) satisfies T(ω) = m s ω(y)(). Proof: K := tsupport ω is closed and K ⊆ ball(y, r) ⊆ ball(y, ρ), so T(ω) = m ∫_M f dH^0 with f(x) := ξ(x)(ω(x)). The function f vanishes outside K (there ω(x) = 0 and ξ(x) is linear), so ∫_M f dH^0 = ∫_{M∩K} f dH^0 (restriction to the closed, hence measurable, set K; no measurability of M is used). Since M ∩ K ⊆ M ∩ ball(y, r) = {y}: if y ∈ K then M ∩ K = {y} and ∫_{{y}} f dH^0 = f(y) H^0({y}) = f(y) = s ω(y)(); if y ∉ K then M ∩ K = ∅, the integral is 0, and s ω(y)() = 0 as well because ω(y) = 0. 3. (Structure of C; parent 4.2.)
 3a. (Local finiteness.) For compact K ⊆ U, H^0(C ∩ K) = ∫_{C∩K} 1 dH^0 ≤ ∫_{C∩K} θ dH^0 < ∞ (θ ≥ 1 on C), so C ∩ K is finite by (F1).
 3b. (Orientation at every point.) By R.orients, the set of points x at which there is no Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt 0 C x Q and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ_R(x)) Q is (H^0⌞C)-null, hence contains no point of C by (F1). So for every x ∈ C there is a subspace Q_x with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt 0 C x Q_x and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ_R(x)) Q_x, and by (F4) ξ_R(x)(α) = s_x α() for all α, with s_x ∈ {1, −1}.
 3c. (Isolated atoms.) If x ∈ C, a > 0, C ∩ closedBall(x, a) = {x}, and ω ∈ 𝒟^0(U) has tsupport ω ⊆ closedBall(x, a), then T(ω) = θ(x) s_x ω(x)(). Indeed the integrand F(z) := θ(z) ξ_R(z)(ω(z)) vanishes outside closedBall(x, a), so ∫_C F dH^0 = ∫_{C ∩ closedBall(x, a)} F dH^0 = ∫_{{x}} F dH^0 = F(x) H^0({x}) = θ(x) s_x ω(x)().

4. (C ∩ ball(y, r) ⊆ {y}; parent 4.3.) Let x ∈ C ∩ ball(y, r) with x ≠ y, and put δ := |x − y| > 0. On the other hand 3c gives T(ω) = θ(x) s_x g(x) = ±θ(x) ≠ 0, since θ(x) ≥ 1. Contradiction.

5. (y ∈ C; parent 4.4.) Suppose y ∉ C; then C ∩ ball(y, r) = ∅ by 4. Let g be as in (F5) for (y, r/2) and ω := g ε₀ ∈ 𝒟^0(U) (closedBall(y, r/2) ⊆ ball(y, r) ⊆ U). Every z ∈ C lies outside ball(y, r) ⊇ tsupport ω, so ω(z) = 0, the integrand of the representation vanishes on C, and T(ω) = 0. But (*) gives T(ω) = m s g(y) = m s ≠ 0. Contradiction. 6. (The competitor; parent 4.5.)
 6a. Define D : 𝒟^0(U) → ℝ by D(ω) := θ(y) ξ_R(y)(ω(y)). D is linear. It is sequentially continuous: if ω_j → 0 in 𝒟^0(U) (all tsupport ω_j in one compact K ⊆ U and all derivatives of ω_j → 0 uniformly on K), then ω_j(y) → 0 (if y ∈ K by uniform convergence of the 0-th derivatives on K; if y ∉ K because ω_j(y) = 0 for all j), so D(ω_j) → 0 by continuity of the linear functional ξ_R(y) on the finite-dimensional space of 0-covectors. Thus D ∈ 𝒟_0(U).
 6b. Let S := T − D ∈ 𝒟_0(U), the contract's difference of currents: S(ω) = T(ω) − D(ω).
 6c. R_S := (C ∖ {y}, θ, ξ_R) is an IMRep in U. Hence the two functions of λ in Definition 1.4 of Ch. 3 (HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt) agree for all small λ > 0 and have the same limit ∫_{Q_x} f dH^0, while the dimension condition finrank Q_x = 0 is unchanged. Thus every point of C ∖ {y} satisfies the orientation condition for R_S, which therefore holds (H^0⌞(C ∖ {y}))-a.e.
 6d. (R_S represents S.) Let ω ∈ 𝒟^0(U) and F(z) := θ(z) ξ_R(z)(ω(z)).
